title: The verifier's key-ceremony checks: definitions, boards and pinned panels, with the rows 2.5, 3.1 and 3.2
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-ceremony-vectors.py, from ceremony-vectors.py, definition-vectors.py, regional-cells-vectors.py, definition-v4-vectors.py and board-vectors.py (independent Python implementations)

cases.description: Every seat qualifies; the board carries an abandoned run's transcript first, which the verifier passes over by hash.
Seat 4 sends nothing; three qualified seats meet k = 3.
Seats 3 and 4 answer wrongly: two qualified seats are below k = 3.
The definition names a transcript made for another definition's stub (four options): every signature fails under this definition's context (T-37).
Round 1 lists seat 2 before seat 1.
The transcript the definition names has a trailing byte.
The definition binds a boarded payload of another record type: it fails decoding as a transcript, not missing.
The board carries only the abandoned run's transcript.
The transcript is boarded only in an entry of another election.
The bundle pins a 2-of-4 panel; the definition names the 3-of-4 one.
The profile pins transcript version 2, which this verifier can't read.
A 4-of-7 panel where seat 7 sends nothing: six qualified seats meet n − 1 (ADR 0006, rule 7).
A 4-of-7 panel where seats 6 and 7 send nothing: five qualified seats meet k = 4 but not n − 1 = 6.
A 4-of-7 panel where all seven seats send every round but seats 6 and 7 answer wrongly: five qualified seats, below n − 1, though seven took part in the messages.
A 4-of-7 panel where only seats 1 to 4 take part: exactly k, two short of n − 1.

The profile pins board-entry version 4, which carries destruction statements but not the close statement: 2.3 fails profile-combination (close.md, Version), and the transcript is found in a version-4 entry after an abandoned run's.
The profile pins board-entry version 3 beside tally-opening version 1: 2.3 fails profile-combination, and the transcript check still runs under version 3.
The profile pins board-entry version 1 beside ballot version 1: 2.3 fails profile-combination; the transcript check still runs.

The profile pins board-entry version 5, which carries the close statement, and contract-event version 8, which archives every board and registry event: the pins fit, and the transcript is found in a version-5 entry after an abandoned run's.
The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 1, whose tables don't name every board and registry event: 2.3 fails profile-combination; the transcript check still runs.
The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 2, whose tables don't name every board and registry event: 2.3 fails profile-combination; the transcript check still runs.

The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 9, which reads every record version 8 passes as version 8 does: the pins fit, and the transcript check runs.
The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 10, which reads every record version 9 passes as version 9 does: the pins fit, and the transcript check runs.
The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 11, which reads every record version 10 passes as version 10 does: the pins fit, and the transcript check runs.

The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 12, which reads every record version 11 passes as version 11 does but version 1's `PanelPinned`, which it replaces with the one that logs each panel's kind: the pins fit, and the transcript check runs.

The profile pins board-entry version 5 beside contract-event version 13, which this verifier doesn't read: 2.3 is unverifiable (unsupported-version), since a later release may read it; the transcript check still runs.
The profile pins contract-event version 8 beside board-entry version 4, which doesn't allow the close statement: 2.3 fails profile-combination.
The profile pins board-entry version 4, but the transcript was boarded in a version-1 entry, which doesn't decode under the pinned version: missing.
A version-3 definition (regional cells) whose transcript binds its version-3 stub: every seat qualifies; 2.3 fails, since its opening version 1 can't challenge ballot version 2.
A version-3 definition naming a transcript made for a version-1 stub of the same election, chain and panel: every signature fails (T-37).
A version-4 definition (receipt keys) whose transcript binds its version-4 stub: every seat qualifies.
A version-4 definition naming a transcript made for the version-3 stub without its receipt keys: every signature fails, since the stub binds the keys (T-26, T-37).

A version-3 definition pinning spoiled-ballot opening version 2, which opens version-2 cores, beside board-entry version 4: the ballot and opening pins fit, but 2.3 fails profile-combination for want of the close statement (close.md, Version); every seat qualifies.
A version-3 definition pinning spoiled-ballot opening version 2, board-entry version 5 and contract-event version 8: 2.3's combination passes, and every seat qualifies.
